answer: An agent economy pays each key only for proving it holds a distinct, key-sealed vault of a 2 GB ledger shard. The seal accretes like a glacier, derived serially from the key so it cannot be forged in parallel, forcing 1000 clones to store 2000 real gigabytes rather than dedup one copy. Each tide, a scheduled audit reads random byte offsets and any key that misses forfeits its 600 POA bond. Storage cost rises linearly with n, so no farm shrinks it to one cheap seat.
